title: Enforcement Decree of the Act on Compensation for Persons Who Performed Special Missions
full_text:
Enforcement Decree of the Act on Compensation for Persons Who Performed Special Missions

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on Compensation for Persons Who Performed Special Missions and matters necessary for its enforcement. <Amended on May 28, 2009>

Article 2 (Definitions)
"Military intelligence units" in Article 2 (1) 2 of the Act on Compensation for Persons Who Performed Special Missions (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means units established and operated by the Armed Forces of the Republic of Korea for purposes such as intelligence gathering of a special nature or form, and excludes units that belonged to foreign armed forces or that were organized before the establishment of military intelligence units and engaged in guerrilla warfare, etc. <Amended on May 28, 2009>

Article 3 (Applicable Periods)
"Periods prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 2 (1) 2 of the Act means the following periods: <Amended on May 2, 2007>
1. Army: From March 6, 1951 through December 31, 2002;
2. Navy: From June 10, 1949 through December 31, 2002;
3. Air Force: From May 15, 1951 through August 31, 1971.

Article 4 (Determination of Eligibility as Persons Who Performed Special Missions, etc.)
(1) Eligibility as a person who performed special missions under Article 2 (2) of the Act shall be determined according to the following criteria: <Amended on October 27, 2010>
1. Persons who performed special missions: Whether the person was assigned and performed a special mission during a period specified in the subparagraphs of Article 3;
2. Persons who received education and training related to special missions: Whether, during a period specified in the subparagraphs of Article 3, the person was hired, enlisted, or selected to perform special missions and completed, at a military intelligence unit, an education and training course as classified in the following items:
(a) Noncommissioned officers (including noncommissioned officer candidates) and enlisted personnel who were on active duty: The basic education and training course under Annex 1;
(b) Persons other than those under item (a): An education and training course related to special missions.
(2) Officers or persons engaged in support duties such as escort shall be recognized as persons who performed special missions only where they are determined to have performed special missions pursuant to paragraph (1) 1.
(3) Deleted. <May 2, 2007>
(4) Where a person recognized as a person who performed special missions under paragraph (1) has been recorded as dead or missing, or has suffered a physical disability, due to any of the following circumstances, the additional merit payment under Article 13 (1) 2, additional special merit payment under Article 13 (2) 2, and special consolation payment under Article 14 shall not be paid:
1. Where the death, disappearance, or disability was caused by the person's intentional act or gross negligence, or arose from a serious violation of relevant statutes and regulations or orders of a superior officer;
2. Where it resulted from an accident or disaster while the person was absent from the special mission;
3. Where it was caused by private conduct unrelated to the performance of special missions, such as horseplay or fighting;
4. Where it resulted from an act of self-harm: Provided, That cases in which the act was unavoidable for the performance of a special mission shall be excluded.

Article 5
Deleted. <October 27, 2010>

Article 6 (Payment Ratios for Bereaved Family Members)
The ratios of compensation payments, etc. payable to siblings and collateral blood relatives of persons who performed special missions pursuant to Article 3 (2) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on May 2, 2007>
1. For siblings: An amount corresponding to 80 percent of the total amount payable to the person who performed special missions: Provided, That, where the person's father or mother was alive at the time of application for consolation compensation payments, etc. under Article 9 (1) of the Act, the amount shall correspond to 90 percent of the total amount payable to the person who performed special missions;
2. For collateral blood relatives: An amount corresponding to 50 percent of the total amount payable to the person who performed special missions.

Article 7 (Composition and Operation of the Compensation Deliberation Committee for Persons Who Performed Special Missions)
(1) Members of the Compensation Deliberation Committee for Persons Who Performed Special Missions under Article 4 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee") shall be commissioned or appointed by the Minister of National Defense, taking gender into account, from among persons falling under the following subparagraphs: <Amended on June 1, 2015; April 11, 2023>
1. Persons who have served as judges, prosecutors, military judicial officers, or attorneys-at-law for at least ten years;
2. Persons who have held positions of assistant professor or higher for at least ten years at schools under subparagraph 1 or 3 of Article 2 of the Higher Education Act;
3. Persons recommended by the heads of their respective institutions from among public officials belonging to the Senior Civil Service of the Ministry of Justice, Ministry of National Defense, and Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
(2) The chairperson of the Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "chairperson") shall be appointed by the Minister of National Defense from among its members. <Amended on June 1, 2015>
(3) The term of office of a member shall be two years and may be renewed consecutively only once.
(4) The chairperson shall represent the Committee and direct its duties.
(5) Where the chairperson is unable to perform the duties of the office due to unavoidable circumstances, a member designated in advance by the chairperson shall act on the chairperson's behalf.
(6) A majority of the incumbent members of the Committee shall constitute a quorum for its meetings, and resolutions shall require the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present.

Article 8 (Matters for Deliberation and Resolution by the Committee)
"Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 4 (2) 4 of the Act means the following matters: <Amended on October 27, 2010>
1. Matters concerning increases or decreases in the service period under Article 11-2 (4);
2. Matters concerning determination of scores and weights under Article 12 and Annex 1-2;
3. Matters concerning reductions in merit payments, special merit payments, and special consolation payments under Articles 13 (3) and 14 (2);
4. Other major matters related to compensation, etc. referred by the chairperson.

Article 9 (Compensation Support Group for Persons Who Performed Special Missions, etc.)
(1) A Compensation Support Group for Persons Who Performed Special Missions shall be established within the Ministry of National Defense to handle the affairs of the Committee. <Amended on May 28, 2009>
(2) The Committee shall have one secretary, who shall concurrently serve as the head of the Compensation Support Group for Persons Who Performed Special Missions. <Newly inserted on May 28, 2009>
(3) The secretary shall be appointed by the Minister of National Defense from among Grade 3 public officials or field-grade officers of the Ministry of National Defense, or the position may be filled by a fixed-term public official. <Amended on June 12, 2006; May 28, 2009; November 20, 2013; June 1, 2015>
(4) The secretary shall handle the affairs of the Committee under orders of the chairperson and may attend and speak at meetings of the Committee. <Amended on May 28, 2009>
(5) Staff positions in the Compensation Support Group for Persons Who Performed Special Missions under paragraph (1) may be filled by public officials dispatched from relevant central administrative agencies and contractual employees. <Amended on May 28, 2009>

Article 10 (Composition of Subcommittees)
(1) The following subcommittees shall be established within the Committee:
1. A Subcommittee for Reviewing Persons Who Performed Special Missions and Bereaved Family Members, to handle the duties under Article 4 (2) 1 of the Act;
2. A Subcommittee for Calculating Compensation Payments, etc., to handle the duties under Article 4 (2) 2 of the Act.
(2) Each subcommittee shall consist of not more than ten members appointed or commissioned by the chairperson from among persons with extensive knowledge and experience and relevant public officials, and the chairperson of each subcommittee shall be appointed by the chairperson from among members of the Committee.
(3) Matters necessary for the operation of each subcommittee shall be determined by the chairperson following a resolution of the Committee.

Article 10-2 (Exclusion, Challenge, and Recusal of Members)
(1) A member (including a member of a subcommittee; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Article and Article 10-3) of the Committee (including a subcommittee; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Article and Article 10-3) shall be excluded from deliberation and resolution on a matter in any of the following cases: <Amended on November 30, 2015>
1. Where the member, the member's spouse, or the member's former spouse is a party to the matter or holds rights jointly with a party to the matter;
2. Where the member is or was a relative of a party to the matter;
3. Where the member is a witness or a person providing a statement under Article 19 (1) of the Act in relation to the matter;
4. Where the member, or a corporation, organization, etc. to which the member belongs, is or was an agent of a party to the matter.
(2) An applicant under Article 10 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "applicant") may file a challenge against a member with the Committee where circumstances make it difficult to expect impartial deliberation and resolution by the member, and the Committee shall decide on the challenge by resolution. In such cases, the member who is the subject of the challenge shall not participate in that resolution.
(3) Where a member falls under any of the grounds for exclusion specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), the member shall notify the Committee of that fact and recuse himself or herself from deliberation and resolution on the matter.
(4) Deleted. <November 30, 2015>

Article 10-3 (Dismissal and Removal of Members)
The authority empowered to commission or appoint members may dismiss a member or terminate the member's commission in any of the following cases:
1. Where the member becomes unable to perform his or her duties due to a mental or physical disability;
2. Where the member has engaged in misconduct in connection with his or her duties;
3. Where the member is deemed unsuitable to serve as a member due to neglect of duties, impairment of dignity, or any other reason;
4. Where the member fails to recuse himself or herself despite falling under any of the subparagraphs of Article 10-2 (1);
5. Where the member expresses that he or she finds it difficult to perform his or her duties.

Article 11 (Allowances, etc.)
(1) Members attending meetings of the Committee or a subcommittee who are not public officials may be paid allowances and travel expenses within budgetary limits.
(2) Witnesses or persons providing statements who appear before the Committee, etc. under Article 19 (1) of the Act may be paid travel expenses and actual expenses within budgetary limits.

Article 11-2 (Calculation of Period of Service)
(1) The period of service of a person who performed special missions, which serves as the basis for payment of compensation under Article 6 (1) of the Act, shall be the number of months from the month in which the person's initial education and training relating to special missions began through the month in which the person ceased to perform special missions or to receive education and training relating thereto due to expiration of a contract, dismissal, discharge from military service, death, disappearance, criminal punishment, reassignment, or any other such reason (the date on which the person so ceased shall hereinafter be referred to as the "date of termination of a special mission").
(2) In calculating the period of service under paragraph (1), the period of service of officers who performed special missions and of noncommissioned officers and civilian military employees assigned to military intelligence units to perform special missions shall be the number of months from the month in which they were assigned to military intelligence units through the month in which their assignments ended.
(3) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where the period of service of a person who performed special missions (excluding a person who performed special missions under paragraph (2)) falls short of the period of service for enlisted soldiers on active duty or the contract period applicable as of the date of termination of a special mission because the special mission was terminated for a reason for which the person was not responsible, the period of service for enlisted soldiers on active duty or the contract period applicable at that time shall be deemed the person's period of service.
(4) Where deemed necessary in light of the type of special mission, form of service, and environment in which the special mission was performed, the period of service of a person who performed special missions may be increased or decreased by an amount not exceeding one-half of the period of service under paragraphs (1) through (3).

Article 12 (Compensation Payments)
(1) A compensation payment shall be the amount calculated by multiplying the base payment amount for the relevant status under subparagraph 1 of Annex 1-2 by the payment ratio for the relevant grade under subparagraph 2 of that Annex and by the period of service under Article 11-2. <Amended on October 27, 2010>
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), for persons who performed special missions who enlisted as noncommissioned officers for short-term service or who served after changing their status to noncommissioned officers for short-term service during education and training, one-third of the base payment amount for the relevant status shall apply to the portion of their service exceeding the period of service for enlisted soldiers on active duty at that time.

Article 13 (Merit Payments and Special Merit Payments)
(1) Merit payments under Article 7 of the Act shall be divided into basic merit payments and additional merit payments and paid as follows: <Amended on May 28, 2009; July 12, 2010>
1. The basic merit payment shall be an amount determined by the Committee in consideration of the circumstances of recruitment or enlistment, the conditions of education and training, actions taken after the date of termination of a special mission, and other relevant factors, within the amount calculated by multiplying 72 times the monthly minimum wage (meaning the amount calculated by multiplying by 226 hours the hourly minimum wage publicly announced by the Minister of Employment and Labor under Article 10 of the Minimum Wage Act as of the date this Decree enters into force) by the payment ratio for the relevant time of recruitment or enlistment under Annex 2.
2. The additional merit payment shall be paid to persons who performed special missions who were recorded as dead or missing or sustained a physical disability during education and training relating to special missions, and their bereaved family members, and its amount shall be calculated by multiplying the base amount for special consolation payments under subparagraph 1 of Annex 4 by the payment ratio for death, disappearance, or the relevant disability grade under Annex 3. In such cases, Article 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the State Compensation Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to disability grades.
(2) Special merit payments under Article 7 of the Act shall be divided into basic special merit payments and additional special merit payments and paid as follows: Provided, That where an officer or a person engaged in support activities, such as escort duties, has performed a special mission, the amount paid out of the special merit payment shall be the amount determined by the Committee under subparagraph 1 in consideration of the time at which special missions were performed, the number of special missions performed, and other relevant factors. <Amended on May 28, 2009>
1. The basic special merit payment shall be the amount calculated by adding, to the basic merit payment under paragraph (1) 1, an amount determined by the Committee in consideration of the time at which special missions were performed, the number of special missions performed, and other relevant factors, within a limit of 75 percent of the base amount for special consolation payments under subparagraph 1 of Annex 4.
2. Paragraph (1) 2 shall apply to the additional special merit payment.
(3) A merit payment or special merit payment may be reduced or withheld from a person deemed to have received compensation under other Acts, such as the Military Accident Compensation Act or the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State, for death or physical disability sustained during education and training relating to special missions. <Amended on May 28, 2009; June 9, 2020>
(4) For any of the following persons, the basic merit payment under paragraph (1) 1 and the basic special merit payment under paragraph (2) 1 may each be paid after a reduction of up to three-fourths of the respective amount, in consideration of the extent of the circumstances specified in the subparagraphs of Article 4 (4), the gravity of the criminal acts specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2-2 (1) of the Act, and other relevant factors: <Added on May 2, 2007; amended on May 28, 2009>
1. A person recognized as a person who performed special missions under any subparagraph of Article 4 (1) who ceased to perform special missions or to receive education and training relating thereto for any reason specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (4) of that Article;
2. A person whom the Committee has again determined to be subject to the Act under Article 2-2 (2) of the Act.
(5) Detailed payment standards for merit payments and special merit payments and other necessary matters shall be determined by the chairperson following deliberation by the Committee. <Amended on May 2, 2007>

Article 14 (Special Consolation Payments)
(1) Special consolation payments under Article 8 of the Act shall be divided into special consolation payments for death and special consolation payments for disability and paid as follows: <Amended on May 28, 2009>
1. A special consolation payment for death shall be paid to the bereaved family members of a person who performed special missions who was recorded as dead or missing in the course of performing a special mission, and its amount shall be determined by the Committee within the base amount for special consolation payments under subparagraph 1 of Annex 4, in consideration of the time of death or disappearance and whether notification of the death or disappearance was delayed.
2. A special consolation payment for disability shall be paid to a person who performed special missions who sustained a physical disability in the course of performing a special mission, and its amount shall be calculated by multiplying the base amount for special consolation payments under subparagraph 1 of Annex 4 by the payment ratio for the relevant disability grade under subparagraph 2 of that Annex. In such cases, Article 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the State Compensation Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to disability grades.
(2) Article 13 (3) shall apply mutatis mutandis where a special consolation payment is reduced or withheld. <Amended on May 28, 2009>

Article 15 (Method of Converting Salaries, Performance Bonuses, etc.)
The conversion of salaries, performance bonuses, etc. to their present value under Article 9 (2) of the Act shall be calculated by reflecting the consumer price index and other indices publicly announced each year by the head of the National Data Agency under subparagraph 2 of Article 3 of the Statistics Act. <Amended on October 23, 2007; October 1, 2025>

Article 16 (Applications for Compensation Payments, etc.)
(1) A person who intends to apply for payment of compensation payments, special merit payments, merit payments, and special consolation payments (hereinafter referred to as “compensation payments, etc.”) pursuant to Article 10 of the Act shall submit to the Committee the applicable application for compensation payments, etc. from among those in attached Forms 1 through 3, accompanied by the following documents. <Amended on June 12, 2006; May 28, 2009; November 2, 2010>
1. Deleted. <June 12, 2006>
2. One copy of a certificate concerning the family relations records of the person who performed special missions or a certified copy of the removed family register (applicable only to bereaved family members);
3. One copy of a designation of a representative of bereaved family members in attached Form 5 (applicable only where a representative of bereaved family members has been designated);
4. One copy of a power of attorney for receipt of compensation payments, etc. in attached Form 7 (applicable only where an application is made through an agent due to emigration, hospitalization, or other unavoidable circumstances);
5. One copy of supporting materials that can substantiate the grounds for the application.
(2) In applying for or receiving compensation payments, etc. under paragraph (1), where the applicants or recipients are bereaved family members and there are two or more heirs to property of the same rank, they shall designate a representative of the bereaved family members using the designation of a representative of bereaved family members in attached Form 5: Provided, That this shall not apply where an agreement cannot be reached among the heirs to property of the same rank. <Amended on May 28, 2009>
(3) Where a person who intends to apply for compensation payments, etc. under paragraph (1) is unable to apply for or receive such payments in person due to emigration, hospitalization, or other unavoidable circumstances, that person may appoint an agent by means of a power of attorney for receipt of compensation payments, etc. in attached Form 7, verified by any of the following persons. <Amended on May 28, 2009>
1. The head of a diplomatic mission abroad, in the case of a stay abroad due to emigration or similar circumstances;
2. The head of the medical institution, in the case of hospitalization;
3. The head of the institution of confinement, in the case of confinement in a prison or similar institution;
4. The head of an eup, myeon, or dong, in other cases.
(4) Where the Committee receives an application for compensation payments, etc. under paragraph (1) and any of the relevant documents specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) are not attached, it shall require the applicant to supplement the application with those documents. <Amended on May 28, 2009>
(5) The Committee that receives an application under paragraph (1) shall verify an extract of the applicant’s resident registration record through the joint use of administrative information pursuant to Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act: Provided, That where the applicant does not consent to such verification, the Committee shall require the applicant to attach the extract. <Amended on November 2, 2010; November 30, 2015>

Article 17 (Additional Amounts for Delayed Decisions on Payment)
Where a decision on payment is made after one year and six months have elapsed from the date on which an application for compensation payments, etc. is made, an amount calculated on the total amount of compensation payments, etc. at the statutory interest rate prescribed in the Civil Act for the period from the day following the date on which one year and six months have elapsed from the date of application through the date of the decision on payment (including the date of a decision upon reconsideration) shall be added to that total amount and paid: Provided, That where the decision on payment is delayed for reasons attributable to the applicant, such as failure to undergo a physical examination without justifiable grounds, the additional amount for delay shall be reduced by an amount not exceeding one half of that additional amount, taking into account the degree of the applicant’s responsibility and other factors, and paid accordingly. <Amended on May 2, 2007>

Article 18 (Ex Officio Re-examination, etc.)
Where special grounds exist, the chairperson may request the relevant subcommittee to re-examine or recalculate a matter examined or calculated by a subcommittee under Article 10.

Article 19 (Compensation Decisions)
When the Committee makes a compensation decision, it shall prepare a written compensation decision in attached Form 8 stating the following matters, and all members present at the Committee meeting shall sign it or affix their names and seals to it. <Amended on November 30, 2015>
1. The applicant’s name, address, and date of birth;
2. The operative part of the decision;
3. The reasons;
4. The date of the decision.

Article 20 (Service of Written Compensation Decisions)
When the Committee makes a compensation decision, it shall retain the original written compensation decision and serve on the applicant two authentic copies of the written compensation decision and a notice of the compensation decision in attached Form 9 or attached Form 10; where the applicant has an agent, it shall serve these on the agent and serve one certified copy of the written compensation decision on the applicant. In such cases, the original written compensation decision may be retained as an electronic document or a digitized document under Article 5 of the Framework Act on Electronic Documents and Transactions. <Amended on November 12, 2024>

Article 21 (Applications for Reconsideration)
A person who intends to apply for reconsideration pursuant to Article 13 of the Act shall submit to the Committee an application for reconsideration in attached Form 11, accompanied by the following documents:
1. One copy of a medical certificate of physical (mental) disability in attached Form 12 issued by a designated hospital (meaning a national general hospital, a hospital affiliated with a medical college anywhere in the country, or a hospital designated by the Committee) (applicable only where an objection is raised to the determination of the disability grade);
2. One copy of other supporting materials that can prove the grounds for reconsideration.

Article 22 (Consent and Claims for Payment)
An applicant who has been served with a notice of a compensation decision pursuant to the former part of Article 20 and wishes to receive compensation payments, etc. shall submit to the Committee a consent and claim form in attached Form 13, accompanied by the following documents. <Amended on November 12, 2024>
1. One authentic copy of the written compensation decision on compensation payments, etc.;
2. One copy of the applicant’s certificate of seal impression, a certificate of personal signature under subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Act on Confirmation of Personal Signature (hereinafter referred to as a “certificate of personal signature”), or a certificate of issuance of an electronic confirmation of personal signature under Article 7 (7) of the same Act (hereinafter referred to as a “certificate of issuance of an electronic confirmation of personal signature”);
3. One copy of the account passbook of a financial institution through which compensation payments, etc. can be received.

Article 23 (Paying Authority)
Compensation payments, etc. determined by the Committee shall be paid by the Committee, but the work involved may be entrusted to the National Treasury.

Article 24 (Time of Payment)
Compensation payments, etc. shall be paid within 30 days from the date on which a claim for payment under Article 22 is made.

Article 25 (Public Notice)
The chairperson shall, within 60 days from the date this Decree enters into force, give public notice in the Official Gazette of the following matters concerning applications for compensation, and shall also give public notice thereof through at least two daily newspapers, public bulletins, an internet website, broadcasting, or similar means. <Amended on November 24, 2020>
1. Persons eligible for compensation;
2. Qualifications of applicants;
3. The authority receiving applications;
4. The application period;
5. Required documents;
6. Standards for calculating compensation payments, etc.;
7. Procedures for deliberation and decisions;
8. Other matters necessary for applications and payment.

Article 26 (Requirements for and Support to Related Organizations)
(1) A nonprofit corporation or organization for which the State may support part of its project expenses or other costs pursuant to Article 21 of the Act shall have the commemoration of persons who performed special missions and similar activities as its purpose of establishment or principal activity, have a record of relevant activities, and be a nonprofit corporation under Article 32 of the Civil Act or a nonprofit nongovernmental organization under Article 2 of the Assistance for Non-Profit, Non-Governmental Organizations Act. <Amended on May 28, 2009>
(2) Where the Committee intends to provide support to an organization pursuant to Article 21 of the Act, such support shall be provided by applying the Assistance for Non-Profit, Non-Governmental Organizations Act mutatis mutandis, but differing levels of support may be provided taking into account its scale and other factors. <Amended on May 28, 2009; January 5, 2021>

Article 27 (Detailed Rules for Implementation)
Matters necessary for the implementation of this Decree shall be prescribed by the chairperson following a resolution of the Committee.
